Scenario fixture: aria-required-attr (roles with a required attr must carry it)

Each target has a stable id of the form ara_case_NN. Scoped to 9 unambiguous, context-independent roles (see rule's implementation notes).

A. Valid

01 — PASS: required attribute is present
06 — PASS: role="heading" with aria-level present
Section title

B. Invalid

02 — FAIL: required attribute is missing entirely
03 — FAIL: required attribute is present but empty/whitespace
07 — FAIL: role="heading" with aria-level missing
Section title
09 — FAIL: role="meter" with aria-valuenow missing (meter has no "indeterminate" concept unlike progressbar)

C. Not applicable (skipped, not counted)

04 — NEUTRAL: role has no required-attrs entry
05 — NEUTRAL: unknown/invalid role token
08 — NEUTRAL: native <h2> with no explicit role (implicit level, not checked by this rule)

Native heading

10 — PASS: role="meter" with aria-valuenow present
11 — NEUTRAL: role="progressbar" with aria-valuenow missing (deliberately NOT required — an indeterminate progressbar legitimately omits it)
12 — PASS: role="combobox" with aria-expanded present but no aria-controls (aria-controls deliberately NOT required unconditionally — only required once the popup is displayed)
13 — NEUTRAL: element has the `hidden` attribute — not currently exposed to the accessibility tree, so a missing required attribute is not flagged (e.g. a custom checkbox whose aria-checked is set on hydration, before it's revealed)
14 — NEUTRAL: element carries aria-busy="true" — author-signaled transient incompleteness (extended by analogy from the WAI-ARIA spec's required-owned-elements escape hatch)
15 — FAIL: role="separator" that is focusable (a splitter the user can move) with no aria-valuenow
16 — NEUTRAL: role="separator" that is not focusable — a structural divider carries no value

End of fixture.
